title: invite-governance-layer: progressive trust scoring, ephemeral invites, and audit hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: current invite handling is brittle: orgs can bypass domain verification via manual invites, there is no progressive trust model for external collaborators, and audit logs lack invite-level context (who created invite, which policy version applied, which SAML assertion triggered it). This ticket implements an "invite governance layer" that centralizes policy evaluation for org/team invites, computes a progressive trust score per invite, issues time-limited ephemeral invites when required, and emits structured audit events compatible with the audit-logging pipeline and RBAC v2 expectations.

Goals:
- Enforce configurable invite policies at org and team scope (allowlist, denylist, domain verification required, SSO-only enforcement).
- Compute a trust score for each invite based on: email domain reputation, prior org relationship, SAML assertion attributes (if present), IP geolocation, and rate limits.
- Automatically downgrade high-risk invites to ephemeral invites (24h TTL) or require admin approval.
- Surface invite policy decisions and trust score in Audit Logs and the Console event stream with structured fields for downstream analysis.
- Integrate with RBAC v2 so invite acceptance can be scoped (guest, member with limited roles) and mapped to role templates.

Non-goals: building a full domain reputation service (we will consume partner signals), and UI polish for the console (backend APIs + basic console table rows only).
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluation API implements org and team level rules (allowlist/denylist/domain-required/sso-only) and returns a decision plus reason codes.
Trust scoring service returns a numeric score (0-100) and categorical risk (low/medium/high) and is used to mark invites ephemeral when risk >= 70.
Invite creation flow accepts an optional SAML assertion payload and factors SAML attributes (email_verified, idp_domain, eduPersonAffiliation) into the score.

Audit logs include structured invite events: invite.create, invite.approve, invite.expire with fields: invite_id, creator_id, policy_version, trust_score, risk_category, scope(org/team), policy_reason_codes.
RBAC v2 mapping ensures accepted invites create principals with role templates compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments and are stored in the new role_binding table.
E2E tests cover allowlist/denylist behavior, SAML-based invites, ephemeral invite TTL enforcement, and audit event emission to the logging pipeline.
Migration plan documented if any schema changes are required and includes backfill window for existing invites.
tasks: Design: finalize policy DSL for invite rules and reason codes (link in related_links).
Backend: implement /api/internal/invite/evaluate endpoint that returns decision + trust_score.
Service: build lightweight trust-scoring service that aggregates signals and exposes proto over gRPC.
Integration: hook invite creation path to call evaluate; enforce ephemeral invite generation and admin approval workflow.
Audit: add structured audit events and ensure downstream Logstash/Kinesis mapping for fields.
RBAC: extend role_binding schema and acceptance path to enforce template-based scoping for invited principals.
Tests: unit + integration tests; QA: run tenant smoke tests, SSO tenants test matrix.
Docs: write developer doc for policy DSL and ops runbook for invite incident response.
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout, canary to 5% orgs, metrics dashboard for invite success/fail, ephemeral acceptance rates.
